title: AGMM short concept (specs/<ID>/concept.json)
description: Structured concept for one short. Every look-defining choice is an ENUMERATED field so tools/concept_check.py can measure sameness against the last 10 approved shorts. Written 6 Oct 2026 after Sam: 'be careful not to make the visuals too similar, they're starting to look the same. we're dropping creativity'. The enums below are the single source of truth (concept_check.py reads them from this file). To add a value, add it here and say why in kit/SPRINT-2026-10-05.md. Definitions are in x-definitions.

derived.description: true = written by tools/concept_backfill.py from CONCEPTS.md / storyboard sheet / spec.json, not by the maker. Allowed only for shorts already in the storyboard registry before the backfill cutoff; pitch is not checked on a derived concept that has no pitch block.

look.description: the build look in registry/moves.json (explainer, cinematic, dossier, newsroom, desktop, softui, chart, evidence, opsmap); informational

beats_fraction.description: share of the short's beats that sit on this ground (the reviewers' '18 of 22 beats'). Verified against the storyboard sheet at submit.

palette.description: 2 to 4 hex colours ordered by screen area; [0] is the ground.

word.description: the spoken word (as it appears in the script) the signature lands on; null only on a derived concept

id.description: the music id exactly as in specs/<ID>/spec.json music.bed

short.description: a recent approved short (in the window) or S52 / P1

subject.description: the named company or person in frame 0; must occur in the script

number_spoken.description: the exact words of the script that speak that number (e.g. 'five hundred million dollars')

word.description: a spoken word of the script the object is tied to

constructed.description: hand-built in code for this story (not a plain text card, a logo or a stock image)

script_quote.description: words copied from the script that carry the factual claim

world_family.desk-paper: a desk, bench, board or sheet of paper/ledger/printout/cards is the surface the story happens on
world_family.ui-screen: software, an app, a phone, a spreadsheet or a console screen is the whole world
world_family.map-plan: a map, floor plan or top-down plan view
world_family.instrument-console: dials, meters, recorders, control or ops rooms, machines you read
world_family.interior-set: a hand-built room or interior (airport, kitchen, library, registry, closet)
world_family.exterior-site: an outdoor or site-scale scene (road, factory floor, hoarding, estate at night, polytunnel)
world_family.unit-wall: a wall or field of countable identical units (badges, pegs, dots, phones, drawers) is the world
world_family.abstract-chart: graph paper, drafting paper or a chart field with diagrammatic objects
world_family.cutaway: a cross-section or cutaway (iceberg, building section)
world_family.photo-led: a real photograph is the ground of the world

x-definitions.ground: ground_bucket = luminance (dark L*<32, mid <68, light) + hue family (coolneutral = neutral, teal, blue; warm = red, orange, amber; green; violet = violet, pink). 'dark-coolneutral' is the navy/charcoal/black-teal bucket every reviewer calls the house look.
x-definitions.hero_device: what carries the idea in the hook and most beats
x-definitions.camera: static = locked frame, objects move; pan = lateral sweep along a wall; travel = the camera follows a path (aisle, line, route); zoom-through = push-in/pull-back/dolly through the scene so scale changes
x-definitions.hook_mechanic: how frame 0 grabs: number-slam (one huge figure + kicker), contrast-pair (two figures set against each other), quote-verbatim, object-in-motion (a built object already working, number secondary), question-prompt, photo-pushin, stamp-verdict, typed-reveal
x-definitions.source_presentation: cream-card = a card with masthead/credit chip that floats over the ground; pinned-clipping = attached to a world surface by tape, pin, peg or clip; on-object = the sourced words are set on a prop of the world (slip, ticket, label, page); screen-window = shown inside an in-world screen or browser window; strip-ticker = lower-third/ticker strip; paper-document = the whole real page at frame size
x-definitions.signature: the hand-built moment that IS the story beat: wave-ignite (a wave lights or kills many units), sort-split (items sorted/diverted/counted), converge-in (items fly into a target), fill-gauge (a level/needle/trace/counter fills), pullback-scale (camera pulls back to show scale), stamp-verdict (a stamp or verdict lands), scan-sweep (a beam/highlighter/reader sweeps), cut-disconnect (unplug/cut/unbolt/seal), travel-path (a pen/pin/camera travels a line), assemble-build (an object assembles or draws itself), layer-merge (two layers slide together), peel-flip (peel/flip/open to reveal), pour-fall (things pour or drop)
